entries.name: Wewak
entries.note: Town: provincial capital of East Sepik and the gateway for Sepik River trips and the Wewak islands; WWII Japanese airbase and surrender site.
entries.reason: Wewak, Kairiru Island, Mushu Island and Cape Wom: base plus three spots; Maprik (about 60 km) would be the fourth but would stretch a town span to about 90 km: not proposed as a destination, all standalone.

entries.name: Vanimo
entries.note: Town: capital of Sandaun Province on the Indonesian border; base for the surf breaks and the coastal headlands.
entries.reason: Vanimo and its surf breaks are two places: standalone.

entries.name: Maprik
entries.note: Town and district: the Maprik area holds the best-known haus tambaran spirit houses; Wikipedia article is the district.
entries.reason: About 60 km inland from Wewak, a district rather than a stop around the town: standalone.

entries.name: Sepik River
entries.coordinates_source: osm:node/2643833870 Angoram (river visitor access point, not the river centroid); Wikipedia article Sepik
entries.note: River: the Sepik, PNG's longest river, visited by motor-canoe and riverboat trips to river villages; a long linear feature, pin at its main visitor access (Wewak, Angoram, Pagwi). Pinned at Angoram, a river-town access point, not the river centroid.
entries.reason: Long river placed at its visitor access (Angoram), not under Wewak: standalone.
entries.pin_flag: Pinned at Angoram, the river's main visitor access (OSM place=town); long feature, not the centroid.

entries.name: Kairiru Island
entries.note: Island: volcanic island 30 minutes by boat off Wewak with waterfalls, snorkelling and natural hot springs (PTPA); guesthouse per Wikivoyage. Wikipedia title 'Kairiru' is the language.
entries.reason: Three spots round Wewak: below four, standalone.

entries.name: Mushu Island
entries.note: Island: coral atoll with a white-sand beach and reef fish, half an hour off Wewak; basic guesthouse. Named Muschu by PTPA. Wikipedia title is the Disney character.

entries.name: Cape Wom
entries.coordinates_source: osm:node/11799415670 monument (Cape Wom Memorial); agrees with Wikipedia within 100 m
entries.note: WWII memorial: peace park where General Adachi signed the Japanese surrender in New Guinea in 1945, with open Japanese tunnels; PTPA calls it the Wom Memorial and Japanese Peace Park.

entries.name: Vanimo Surf Breaks
entries.coordinates_source: osm:node/1250713739 natural=cape Vanimo Point (area point; surf breaks not named in any source)
entries.note: Surf breaks: consistent reef and point breaks west of Vanimo, up to 3 m, best September to March (Wikivoyage); experienced surfers only.

reviews.name: Angoram
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) names it as a road-accessible river village, the lower-Sepik start of trips.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: main road gateway to the Sepik by road from Wewak, a harbour-town style stop. Against: no sight or activity listed, one source, mostly a launching point.

reviews.name: Ambunti
reviews.reason: Rule 1: PTPA Momase names it only as the festival host; Remote Lands lists it as a Sepik region hub. Upper Sepik base for crocodile and bird trips.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: recognised upper-Sepik village a guide treats as a destination. Against: the counted mention is the festival (an event), no permanent sight described.

reviews.name: Pagwi
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) lists it as a road-accessible river village near the Chambri Lakes.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: road access point for Middle Sepik canoe trips. Against: a transit village with guesthouses, no sight described.

reviews.name: Chambri Lakes
reviews.reason: Rule 1: re-looked; PTPA's Sepik Adventure Tours business listing and tour itineraries (Aibom pottery, Wombun haus tambaran) name it as a stop, but no editorial counted page found.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: genuine river-trip stop with a pottery village. Against: sourcing is operator material only; seasonal water level.

reviews.name: Robuin Island
reviews.reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Sepik and Remote Lands both name it, as an uninhabited WWII fuel-dump island off Wewak.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: two counted sources and a day-trip island like Kairiru and Mushu. Against: uninhabited, owned by Wom village, no facilities and no coordinates found; needs landowner permission.

reviews.name: Wuvulu Island
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) for diving. Administratively Manus Province: belongs to the islands (Manus) region, not this one.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: Cousteau-cited diving, a real destination. Against: one source here and outside this region; route to the Manus pass.

reviews.name: Mission Hill
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (PTPA Momase 'main attractions'), no description found.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a lookout PTPA lists as a main Wewak attraction. Against: a single listing, no description, short visit.

reviews.name: Vanimo Headlands
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands 'The Headland'): limestone peninsula with beaches and snorkelling; overlaps the Vanimo Surf Breaks pin at Vanimo Point.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: named experience (beaches, snorkelling, villages). Against: one source, an area not a site, near-duplicate pin with Vanimo Surf Breaks.

reviews.name: Palimbei
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands, Palambe village haus tambaran and sago demonstration), no coordinates and spelling varies.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a named village visit with a haus tambaran. Against: one operator-style source, no pin, only via tour.

reviews.name: Mindimbit
reviews.reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands): Iatmul village known for carved moon-faced figures and masks, with a men's spirit house.
reviews.skeptic_objection: For: a named craft village visit. Against: single source, tour access only.

note: PNG has no existing destinations or spots. Placement run jointly for all nine regions; proposed destinations are in curation/png/destinations-proposed.json.
